top_signals.title: Mexico’s Richest Man Sells $1.15 Billion in Oil Stocks
top_signals.summary: Carlos Slim has sold more than $1.15 billion of U.S. oil stocks this year as the Iran war sends crude prices and energy shares higher. The Mexican billionaire has cut his stakes in PBF Energy and Talos Energy roughly in half, yet the shares he still owns are worth about $1.4 billion—roughly what his holdings were worth in January. Much of his estimated $124 billion fortune is tied to telecommunications giant América Móvil. Slim, the richest man in Mexico, collected around $820 million selling PBF shares over more than 100 trading…

top_signals.title: Europe to Release 42 Million Barrels of Oil
top_signals.summary: Europe will release 42 million barrels of emergency oil stocks over the next three months, half of it diesel, as governments try to bring down fuel prices before winter, French Economy Minister Roland Lescure said Thursday. France's share includes 10 million barrels of diesel, which Lescure said will begin reaching the market in the coming days. The fuel will be supplied at cost, with Lescure forecasting a reduction of 12 to 18 cents per liter. He expects prices to respond as early as next week. top_signals.summary: Lenders to Partners Group-backed Rovensa are looking to offload the debt of the Iberian agricultural products maker as the firm burns through cash.

top_signals.title: Mixed outlook for energy expenditures this winter
top_signals.summary: We expect energy expenditures this winter to vary because of diverging trends in energy prices among fuels and regional variation in forecast temperatures. We expect that lower prices for natural gas and propane will drive decreases in expenditures this year for the half of U.S. households heating with those fuels. Higher prices for electricity and heating oil drive increased expenditures for households heating with those fuels in our forecast.
